unit-bee4.srcName: Spelling Bee Words — 2026-27 Scripps 'Two Bee' 4th Grade Study List (Drive)
unit-bee4.source: Scripps National Spelling Bee, 2026-27 Two Bee Study Words for Fourth Grade — official 50-word study list (Drive)

summary.text: List 4 of River's Spelling Bee study words: inferior, December, duration, dictionary, business, reinstate, examine, versus, lullaby, opposite, tissues, marlin.

why.text: This is the real Scripps "Two Bee" fourth-grade word list — the words a school spelling bee actually draws from. Saying each word aloud, letter by letter, is the same skill a real bee tests, not just recognizing the word on a page.

objectives.text: Spell every word on this list correctly, letter by letter, from hearing it alone.
State each word's meaning in your own words.

parentNote.text: Built from "Spelling Bee Words", the 2026-27 Scripps Two Bee fourth-grade study list you added to her Drive folder. All 50 official words are split across four lessons; every definition and example sentence here was written fresh, since the source is a bare word list with no definitions to copy. The flashcards use the honeycomb "bee" look, and each lesson also opens the Spelling Bee voice game — hear it, spell it aloud letter by letter.

nextUp.text: Cards first to learn the meanings, then the Spelling Bee game to practice saying the letters aloud.

cards.def:
**Lower in rank, status, or quality compared to something or someone else.**
• The reviewer said the cheap copy felt inferior to the original.
cards.hint: IN- + FERIOR — it pairs with its opposite, "superior".

cards.def:
**The twelfth and final month of the year, marking the start of winter in the Northern Hemisphere.**
• Snow usually starts falling here by mid-December.
cards.hint: Capital D, then DE- + CEM- + -BER — "cem" rhymes with "gem".

cards.def:
**The length of time that something lasts or continues.**
• The movie's duration was just over two hours.

**A reference book that lists words in alphabetical order along with their meanings and pronunciations.**
• She looked up the unfamiliar word in the dictionary.

**A person's regular work or trade, or an organization that makes, buys, or sells goods and services.**
• Their family business has sold bicycles for three generations.
cards.hint: BUSI- (from "busy") + -NESS — the U makes an "i" sound.

cards.def:
**To restore someone or something to a former position, condition, or state.**
• The committee voted to reinstate the canceled holiday.
cards.hint: RE- + IN- + STATE — three small words joined.

cards.def:
**To inspect something carefully and in detail, or to test someone's knowledge.**
• The doctor took a moment to examine the small cut on her hand.
cards.hint: EX- + AMINE, one M — like "exam" with -ine added.

cards.def:
**Against, used to describe two sides opposing each other, especially in a contest, game, or legal case.**
• Friday's game is the home team versus their biggest rivals.
cards.hint: VERSUS is its own whole word — one S in the middle, one at the end.

cards.def:
**A soft, soothing song sung to help a baby or young child fall asleep.**
• Her grandmother hummed the same lullaby every night before bed.

**Situated on the other side of something, or completely different in nature or direction.**
• North is the exact opposite direction from south.

**Soft, absorbent paper used for wiping or blowing the nose, or the biological material that makes up living things.**
• He grabbed a box of tissues before his nose started running.
cards.hint: TISSUE keeps its U even though you do not hear it — TIS- + -SUE.

cards.def:
**A large, fast ocean fish with a long, spear-shaped upper jaw, prized by sport fishers.**
• The fishing boat's crew spotted a marlin leaping near the horizon.

questions.q: Spell the word: lower in rank, status, or quality compared to something or someone else.
questions.hint: IN- + FERIOR — it pairs with its opposite, "superior".
steps: Four syllables: in, fe, ri, or.

ex.tip: "Inferior" and "superior" share the same -FERIOR/-PERIOR-style ending pattern.

questions.q: Spell the word: the twelfth and final month of the year, marking the start of winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
questions.hint: Capital D, then DE- + CEM- + -BER — "cem" rhymes with "gem".

ex.tip: Months are always capitalized, and the middle syllable rhymes with "gem" and "stem".

questions.q: Spell the word: the length of time that something lasts or continues.

ex.tip: The -TION ending always sounds like "shun" — a pattern shared with "nation" and "station".

questions.q: Spell the word: a reference book that lists words in alphabetical order along with their meanings and pronunciations.
steps: Four syllables: dic, tion, a, ry.

ex.tip: "Diction" means the way words are said — a dictionary is where you look them up.

questions.q: Spell the word: a person's regular work or trade, or an organization that makes, buys, or sells goods and services.
questions.hint: BUSI- (from "busy") + -NESS — the U makes an "i" sound.
steps: Three syllables: busi, ness — said as two: BIZ-nis.

ex.tip: It looks like it should say "BUS-i-ness", but it comes from "busy" and sounds like "BIZ-nis".

questions.q: Spell the word: to restore someone or something to a former position, condition, or state.
questions.hint: RE- + IN- + STATE — three small words joined.
steps: Finish with S-T-A-T-E, the word "state" itself.

ex.tip: "State" keeps its own spelling exactly, with RE- and IN- stacked in front.

questions.q: Spell the word: to inspect something carefully and in detail, or to test someone's knowledge.
questions.hint: EX- + AMINE, one M — like "exam" with -ine added.

ex.tip: "Exam" is short for "examination" — this word is the verb they both come from.

questions.q: Spell the word: against, used to describe two sides opposing each other, especially in a contest, game, or legal case.
questions.hint: VERSUS is its own whole word — one S in the middle, one at the end.
steps: V-E-R-S, one S in the middle.

ex.tip: It is a full word on its own — not an abbreviation, even though it is often shortened to "vs." in print.

questions.q: Spell the word: a soft, soothing song sung to help a baby or young child fall asleep.
steps: L-U-L-L, double L, from the word "lull".

ex.tip: "Lull" means to calm gently — exactly what a lullaby does.

questions.q: Spell the word: situated on the other side of something, or completely different in nature or direction.

ex.tip: The double P is the part most often forgotten — say "op-po" slowly to hear both.

questions.q: Spell the word: soft, absorbent paper used for wiping or blowing the nose, or the biological material that makes up living things.
questions.hint: TISSUE keeps its U even though you do not hear it — TIS- + -SUE.
steps: The U is silent but still there.
Add S for the plural: tissues.

ex.tip: "Tissue" has a silent U right before the E — easy to drop by accident.

questions.q: Spell the word: a large, fast ocean fish with a long, spear-shaped upper jaw, prized by sport fishers.

ex.tip: Not "marlyn" or "marlen" — it ends plainly in -LIN.
